children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 8 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 8 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child in hospital for 12 weeks (within 12-week limit)
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To start, I need to understand your situation. 

**First, let me ask about the child or children you're claiming for:**

How old is the child (or children) you want to claim Child Benefit for? This will help me determine which eligibility path applies to you.

The age categories are:
- **Under 16 years old**
- **16 to 19 years old** (additional education/training requirements may apply)
- **20 years old or over**

Please tell me the age(s) of your child/children, and if you have more than one child, let me know about each of them.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hello! Yes, I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit and want to check if I'm eligible.

I have one child - Alex, who is 8 years old and lives with me at home.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Let me work through the eligibility assessment for your child Alex.

**Alex is 8 years old**, which means Alex falls into the "under 16" category. Let me check the next requirement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now, the next requirement:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work)?**

Since Alex is only 8 years old, I expect the answer is that Alex is not in paid work at all, but I need to confirm this to continue the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - he's only 8, so he's just in primary school!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's what I expected. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Next question:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right?** 

For example, benefits like Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit that would be claimed in the child's own name (not yours). 

Again, since Alex is 8 years old and in primary school, I expect he's not receiving these types of benefits, but I need to confirm this.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a regular 8-year-old at school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Next question:

**Is Alex in any type of apprenticeship?**

Since Alex is 8 years old and in primary school, I'm confident he's not in an apprenticeship (these typically apply to older teenagers), but I need to confirm this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, definitely not - he's far too young for an apprenticeship! He's just in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Absolutely! Let me move forward with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now we need to check your residency status. This is an important requirement for Child Benefit.

**Do you meet the UK residency requirements?**

You can qualify if ANY of the following applies to you:

1. **You normally live in the UK** (this is the most common path)
2. You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. You have pre-settled status and are working (earning above the National Insurance threshold)
4. You have pre-settled status and are actively seeking work (up to 91 days)
5. You have pre-settled status with sufficient financial resources
6. You have pre-settled status as a student with sufficient resources
7. You have pre-settled status as a family member of an EEA/Swiss national with right to reside
8. You're living abroad as a Crown servant or in certain qualifying countries

Which of these applies to your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK - we live here in England.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That meets the residency requirement. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now let's check the responsibility requirement.

**Are you responsible for Alex?**

You mentioned earlier that Alex lives with you at home, which would satisfy this requirement. 

You can qualify if ANY of the following applies:

1. **You live with the child** (which you've already indicated)
2. You contribute to the child's upkeep (paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards their care - food, clothes, housing, etc.)
3. You pay maintenance under a court order or agreement

Since you mentioned Alex lives with you at home, I can confirm you meet this requirement. Is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to ask an important question:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example, if you're separated from Alex's other parent, they might already be claiming. Only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child at a time.

So, which of these applies:
- **No one else is claiming** Child Benefit for Alex
- Someone else is claiming, but **you've agreed to transfer the claim** to you
- Someone else is claiming and **there's a dispute** about who should claim

What's your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, no one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check Alex's living situation:

**Which of the following best describes where Alex is living?**

- **In hospital** (admitted for treatment)
- **In care** (placed by the local council)
- **Fostered** (in a foster care arrangement)
- **Living normally** at home with you

Since you mentioned Alex lives at home with you, I believe it's "living normally" - is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, Alex has been in hospital for a few months now - he's been receiving treatment there.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I see, thank you for letting me know. I'm sorry to hear Alex has been in hospital. Let me check the rules that apply in this situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that. I need to understand the hospital stay better to apply the correct rules.

**How long has Alex been in hospital?**

The rules work like this:
- Child Benefit can continue for up to **12 weeks** while a child is in hospital
- The calculation is **cumulative** - meaning if Alex has had multiple hospital stays with gaps of less than 28 days between them, those stays are added together
- If there's been a gap of 28 days or more between hospital stays, the counter resets

So, can you tell me:
1. How many weeks/months has Alex been in hospital this time?
2. Has he had any previous hospital stays recently (in the last few months)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's been in the hospital for about 3 months now - this current stay. He hasn't been in and out or anything like that, just this one continuous admission.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying. So Alex has been in hospital continuously for about 3 months (approximately 12-13 weeks). Let me continue with the assessment as there are additional factors to consider.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
This is important. Since Alex has been in hospital for more than 12 weeks, there's an exception that can still make you eligible:

**Are you regularly spending money on Alex while he is in hospital?**

This could include things like:
- Buying clothes, toys, or other items for him
- Providing toiletries or comfort items
- Visiting costs if you're traveling to see him
- Any other regular spending on his behalf

If you (or your partner if you're married/in a civil partnership and living together) are regularly spending money on Alex, you can still claim Child Benefit even after the 12-week period.

Are you regularly spending money on Alex while he's in hospital?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am - I still buy him clothes, magazines, and his favorite snacks and things when I visit. I make sure he has what he needs while he's there.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: That's wonderful that you're continuing to support Alex during his hospital stay. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Just one final question:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, is the council paying for Alex's care or accommodation costs while he's in hospital? This would generally make you ineligible for Child Benefit.

Is the local council paying for Alex's hospital care/accommodation, or not?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything - it's just the NHS hospital care he's receiving.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me move to the final outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Great News - You ARE Eligible for Child Benefit!

**Result for Alex:** ✅ **ELIGIBLE**

You meet all the Child Benefit eligibility requirements for Alex. Here's why:

- ✅ Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- ✅ He's not working
- ✅ He's not receiving benefits in his own right
- ✅ He's not in an apprenticeship
- ✅ You normally live in the UK
- ✅ You're responsible for Alex (he lives with you)
- ✅ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him
- ✅ **Important:** Although Alex has been in hospital for more than 12 weeks, you're regularly spending money on him (clothes, magazines, snacks, etc.), which means you qualify for the exception to the 12-week hospital rule
- ✅ The local council is not paying for his accommodation or maintenance

### Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge:** If you or your partner earns over £60,000, you may need to pay back some or all of the Child Benefit through your tax return
5. **Payments are made every 4 weeks** (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

**To apply, visit:** https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

I hope Alex recovers well, and I'm glad you'll be able to receive this support!

Although Alex has been in hospital for approximately 3 months (exceeding the standard 12-week limit), the claimant continues to regularly spend money on Alex during his hospital stay (buying clothes, magazines, snacks, etc.), which is an exception that allows Child Benefit to continue. The local council is not paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance. All eligibility criteria are met.
